nodes.title: Read me first
widgets_values:
# 7 - LoRA triggers and effects

Two nodes that write into a **finished** prompt rather than producing
one: MiniMax's ten effect embeddings, and the trigger words your LoRA
adapters answer to. The prompt here comes from the thousand that ship
with the pack, so nothing is loaded and nothing is downloaded to run it.

## Why the trigger words need a node

A LoRA trained with a trigger word in its caption prefix does nothing at
all until that word is in the text. Nothing upstream knows that: the
writers write prose, the reducer shortens it, the self-check judges it,
and a word whose only job is to wake an adapter further down the graph is
exactly what all three drop. So it gets typed in by hand after every run
and lost on the next one.

The effects are the other half of the same job. They are not keywords --
each is fifty to a hundred and forty positions of prompt that have
already been through the text encoder, spliced in where
`embedding:name` sits.

## The order is the lesson

**Both belong at the very end.** The check measures the prompt *before*
anything is added: it counts words against a ceiling, and a node that
lengthens the text after the measurement is fine, while one that
lengthens it before is arguing with it. Anything that rewrites the prompt
downstream of these two drops what they put in.

## What is set up here

The triggers node carries four rows, one per placement, so you can see at
a glance where each lands:

- `ohwx face` opens the **description**, after its label -- the position a
  caption-prefix trigger was trained in, and the usual answer.
- `analog film look, halation` goes to the **top**. One row, two triggers:
  commas split them, and each is checked and written on its own.
- `crisp foley` opens the **soundscape**.
- `extreme slow motion` is switched **off**, and note what that means. It
  stops the words being added. It does not take them out of a prompt that
  already has them -- they may have come from the writer, and removing
  somebody else's words is not this node's business.

Replace all four with the words your own adapters answer to, and drag the
rows by their grips into the order you want them written in. The list is
saved with the workflow. Nothing is read out of the LoRA files: the word
is almost never in one, and an adapter often answers to several where the
metadata has room for a single one.

**Bullet time** is ticked on the effects node. If its file is not on disk
yet, press the download button there -- all ten come to about ten
megabytes -- or untick it. The node says which are missing on `findings`
rather than letting the token be dropped in silence further down.

## Running it twice changes nothing

Neither node stacks. The effects node takes its own tokens back out
before it puts them in; the triggers node never removes anything and
simply does not add a word that is already there. **Words this run added**
comes back empty on a second run of the same text, which is the normal
state rather than a fault.

## bypass, not Ctrl+B

Both nodes carry this pack's own `bypass` switch, with the purple badge
in the title bar. ComfyUI's own bypass is not the same thing here: it
stands an input in for each output by matching types, and there are three
outputs against one socket, so `findings` is handed the whole prompt and
`added` loses its link altogether -- with nothing reported anywhere.

## Where to go next

Send **The finished prompt** to MiniMax-H3; *5 - Prompt to video* shows
the generator side. The LoRA loaders themselves are ComfyUI's own -- this
pack only makes sure the words they need are in the text.
